la:adj:rebellis.gloss: That makes war anew, waging war again; insurgent, rebellious.
senses: That makes war anew, waging war again; insurgent, rebellious.
la:adj:rebellis.html:
rĕbellis, is, adj.
id.
,
that makes war afresh, insurgent, rebellious (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Lit.: rebelles Aeneadae,: Gallus,: Numidae,: regio rebellis et indomita,: colonia,: motus,.— Subst.: rĕbelles, ium, m., rebels, ; ; ; .—
Trop.: rebellis amor,: flammae seditione rogi,: cervix,: animi,.

la:verb:rebello.gloss: to renew war, to wage war again
senses: to renew war, to wage war again
la:verb:rebello.html:
rĕ-bello, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n.,
to wage war again (said of the conquered), to make an insurrection, to revolt, rebel (mostly postAug.; not in Cic. or Cæs.; syn.: descisco).
Lit.: Volsci rebellarunt,; ; ; 8, 14, 5: crebrius,; (but very dub. ap. ).—Poet.: tauro mutatus membra rebello,renew the combat,; so .—
Trop.: credunt rebellare quae curaverint vitia,to break out again,: rebellat saepe umor, offers resistance (to writing), ; cf.: Pudor rebellat,resists,: ille divus callidi monstri cinis in nos rebellat,i. e. the sphinx,.

la:noun:rebellio.gloss: A renewal of war; rebellion, insurgency, revolt.
senses: A renewal of war; rebellion, insurgency, revolt.
la:noun:rebellio.html:
rĕbellĭo, ōnis, f.
id.
,
a renewal of war (by the conquered party), a revolt, rebellion (good prose; cf.: defectio, seditio): rebellio facta post deditionem,; so, facere,; 4, 38: parare,: coeptare,: comprimere,: ad rebellionem spectare,: ad rebellionem compellere,: nihil rebellionis timere,: Germaniae,: trium principum,.— In plur.: multis Carthaginiensium rebellionibus, * .

la:noun:rebellium.gloss: a renewal of war, revolt, rebellion
senses: a renewal of war, revolt, rebellion
la:noun:rebellium.html:
rĕbellĭum, ii, n.
id.
,
a renewal of war, revolt, rebellion (a collat. form for rebellio, like consortium for consortio, contagium for contagio, etc.): qui pacatos ad rebellium incitasset, Gronov. (dub.; Weissenb. rebellandum).
